entries.name: Frost Reckoning
entries.displayTemplate: {value} bonus damage against a frozen target
entries.notes: NEW family, the FIRST payoff half `pairings.json` names ('atom.chill-punisher') to actually exist in the 98-family namespace -- spec-distribution-planner.md's own DECIDED-but-unexecuted deliverable, closed here. Enabler: `atom.freezing` (g-affliction.json, status=freeze, a real working UnityCc row, not one of the inert/partial appliers). Priced and banded (`resource.delta`, `powerBand: low`, params identical to `atom.hit-followthrough`'s own shape in g-on-hit.json) as an UNCONDITIONAL on-hit bonus, because the family-authoring layer (this schema) has no gate/predicate field -- confirmed by reading AtomCompiler.cs and every existing family file: `when` here is a bare event-hook string (`OnDamageDealt`), never the `{predicate, chance, icd_ms}` shape `AtomRow.WhenJson` supports at the compiled-atom-row layer. The engine already has a real, tested leaf for this exact check -- `PredicateNode.LeafId.HasStatus` (`src/FusionRpg.Core/Effects/Atoms/PredicateNode.cs:34`) -- but no shipped content anywhere uses it yet, and wiring a family-authoring-time predicate through to it is real, separate, unscoped work. Until that lands this family is priced honestly as what it does today (an unconditional bonus, same cost as `hit-followthrough`), not what its name promises -- the same shape `atom.entangling`'s own note already uses for its own binds-nowhere gap. `EnablerPayoffPairings` itself does not require runtime status-gating to be real: it is a content-PLANNING table only (co-occurrence of payoff+enabler in the same brief pool), never a predicate-tree parse, so this family unblocks the pairing tier today regardless of when the predicate wiring lands.

entries.name: Blighted Reckoning
entries.displayTemplate: {value} bonus damage against an afflicted target
entries.notes: NEW family, the SECOND payoff half `pairings.json` names ('atom.rot-punisher') to actually exist in the 98-family namespace -- same deliverable as `atom.chill-punisher` above, same file, same reasoning for `kindId`/`powerBand`/the honest unconditional-today pricing, same `PredicateNode.HasStatus` real-but-unwired mechanism. Enablers (four, matching the EXISTING pairings.json many-to-one shape for this exact key -- 'rot-punisher -> [rot-applier, blight-applier]' before this rewrite): `atom.venomous` (poison), `atom.withering` (wither, g-affliction.json's own 'fully functional... no missing payload half'), `atom.bloodletting` (leech, PARTIAL -- tick half only, still real), `atom.sporing` (spore, base tick real, spread mechanic dormant). Deliberately excludes `atom.entangling` (kelp) -- declared INERT in g-affliction.json's own note, 'binds nowhere' at runtime -- and `atom.mesmerizing` (hypno) -- thematically CC, not affliction/DoT, left unpaired rather than forced into a mismatched group; both remain legally usable, real, un-payoff'd enablers, named here rather than silently dropped.
